sanskrit: tvayi vatse parāśvasya brāhmaṇasyābhirādhanam tan me vākyaṃ na mithyā tvaṃ kartum arhasi karhi cit
english: On you, my child, rests the honour of serving this brahmin, the support of our life. That word of mine you must never make false at any time.

sanskrit: ayaṃ tapasvī bhagavān svādhyāyaniyato dvijaḥ yad yad brūyān mahātejās tat tad deyam amatsarāt
english: This ascetic lord, this twice-born devoted to his studies, this man of great splendour — whatever he asks, all of it must be given ungrudgingly.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā hi paraṃ tejo brāhmaṇā hi paraṃ tapaḥ brāhmaṇānāṃ namaskāraiḥ sūryo divi virājate
english: Brahmins are the highest splendour; brahmins are the highest austerity. It is by obeisance to brahmins that the sun shines in the sky.

sanskrit: amānayan hi mānārhān vātāpiś ca mahāsuraḥ nihato brahmadaṇḍena tālajaṅghas tathaiva ca
english: For Vātāpi the great demon, who dishonoured those worthy of honour, was slain by the staff of brahmic power — and Tālajaṅgha likewise.

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ vatse mahābhāra āhitas tvayi sāṃpratam tvaṃ sadā niyatā kuryā brāhmaṇasyābhirādhanam
english: This great burden, my child, has now been placed upon you. You must always, with self-restraint, perform the honouring of this brahmin.

sanskrit: jānāmi praṇidhānaṃ te bālyāt prabhṛti nandini brāhmaṇeṣv iha sarveṣu gurubandhuṣu caiva ha
english: I know your devotion since childhood, my dear daughter, toward all brahmins and toward teachers and kinsmen alike.

sanskrit: tathā preṣyeṣu sarveṣu mitrasaṃbandhimātṛṣu mayi caiva yathāvat tvaṃ sarvam ādṛtya vartase
english: Likewise toward all servants, toward friends, relations, and mothers, and toward me as well — you have always conducted yourself with full respect.

sanskrit: na hy atuṣṭo jano 'stīha pure cāntaḥpure ca te samyagvṛttyānavadyāṅgi tava bhṛtyajaneṣv api
english: There is no dissatisfied person in this city or in the inner apartments with regard to you, O blameless one, and not even among your servants, owing to your proper conduct.

sanskrit: saṃdeṣṭavyāṃ tu manye tvāṃ dvijātiṃ kopanaṃ prati pṛthe bāleti kṛtvā vai sutā cāsi mameti ca
english: Yet I think I must instruct you regarding this irascible twice-born, O Pṛthā — bearing in mind that you are young and that you are my daughter.

sanskrit: vṛṣṇīnāṃ tvaṃ kule jātā śūrasya dayitā sutā dattā prītimatā mahyaṃ pitrā bālā purā svayam
english: You were born in the clan of the Vṛṣṇis, the beloved daughter of Śūra; as a child you were given to me long ago by your father himself out of affection.

sanskrit: vasudevasya bhaginī sutānāṃ pravarā mama agryam agre pratijñāya tenāsi duhitā mama
english: Sister of Vasudeva, foremost among children — your father having pledged his first child at the outset, you became my daughter.

sanskrit: tādṛśe hi kule jātā kule caiva vivardhitā sukhāt sukham anuprāptā hradād dhradam ivāgatā
english: Born in such a lineage and raised in such a lineage, you have moved from comfort to comfort, as if passing from one lake to another.

sanskrit: dauṣkuleyā viśeṣeṇa kathaṃ cit pragrahaṃ gatāḥ bālabhāvād vikurvanti prāyaśaḥ pramadāḥ śubhe
english: Women who have come from inferior families and by some chance risen to prosperity generally misbehave in their youth, O fair one.

sanskrit: pṛthe rājakule janma rūpaṃ cādbhutadarśanam tena tenāsi saṃpannā samupetā ca bhāminī
english: But you, Pṛthā, were born in a royal family, and your beauty is marvellous to behold — endowed with all of these, you are well-graced, O passionate one.

sanskrit: sā tvaṃ darpaṃ parityajya dambhaṃ mānaṃ ca bhāmini ārādhya varadaṃ vipraṃ śreyasā yokṣyase pṛthe
english: Therefore, O spirited one, abandoning pride, deceit, and arrogance, serve this brahmin who grants boons, and you shall be yoked to prosperity, O Pṛthā.

sanskrit: evaṃ prāpsyasi kalyāṇi kalyāṇam anaghe dhruvam kopite tu dvijaśreṣṭhe kṛtsnaṃ dahyeta me kulam
english: In this way you will surely attain good fortune, O auspicious and sinless one. But if this best of twice-born is angered, my entire lineage could be consumed.

sanskrit: kunty uvāca brāhmaṇaṃ yantritā rājan upasthāsyāmi pūjayā yathāpratijñaṃ rājendra na ca mithyā bravīmy aham
english: Kuntī said: Bound by duty, O king, I shall attend upon the brahmin with reverence as promised, O lord of kings — I do not speak falsely.

sanskrit: eṣa caiva svabhāvo me pūjayeyaṃ dvijān iti tava caiva priyaṃ kāryaṃ śreyaś caitat paraṃ mama
english: This is moreover my own nature — to honour the twice-born. And this is what is dear to you and what is my highest good.

sanskrit: yady evaiṣyati sāyāhne yadi prātar atho niśi yady ardharātre bhagavān na me kopaṃ kariṣyati
english: Whether he comes in the evening, in the morning, or at night, or even at midnight — the reverend one shall not find cause to be angry with me.

sanskrit: lābho mamaiṣa rājendra yad vai pūjayatī dvijān ādeśe tava tiṣṭhantī hitaṃ kuryāṃ narottama
english: This is my own gain, O lord of kings, that by honouring brahmins while abiding in your command, I shall be doing what is beneficial — O best of men.

sanskrit: visrabdho bhava rājendra na vyalīkaṃ dvijottamaḥ vasan prāpsyati te gehe satyam etad bravīmi te
english: Be at ease, O lord of kings — the best of twice-born shall find no offence while dwelling in your house. I tell you this truly.

sanskrit: yat priyaṃ ca dvijasyāsya hitaṃ caiva tavānagha yatiṣyāmi tathā rājan vyetu te mānaso jvaraḥ
english: Whatever is pleasing and beneficial to this brahmin and to you, O sinless one, I shall strive for — O king, let the fever of your mind pass.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā hi mahābhāgāḥ pūjitāḥ pṛthivīpate tāraṇāya samarthāḥ syur viparīte vadhāya ca
english: For brahmins of great fortune, when honoured, O lord of the earth, are capable of causing liberation — but in the opposite case, of causing destruction.

sanskrit: sāham etad vijānantī toṣayiṣye dvijottamam na matkṛte vyathāṃ rājan prāpsyasi dvijasattamāt
english: Knowing this, I shall satisfy this best of twice-born. You shall suffer no distress on my account from this best of brahmins, O king.

sanskrit: aparādhe hi rājendra rājñām aśreyase dvijāḥ bhavanti cyavano yadvat sukanyāyāḥ kṛte purā
english: For when kings transgress, brahmins bring misfortune, O lord of kings — as Cyavana did in the matter of Sukanyā in former times.

sanskrit: niyamena pareṇāham upasthāsye dvijottamam yathā tvayā narendredaṃ bhāṣitaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ prati
english: With the utmost restraint I shall attend upon this best of twice-born, exactly as you, O best of lords of men, have spoken concerning the brahmin.

sanskrit: rājovāca evam etat tvayā bhadre kartavyam aviśaṅkayā maddhitārthaṃ kulārthaṃ ca tathātmārthaṃ ca nandini
english: The king said: This is indeed what you must do, my good daughter, without hesitation — for my welfare, for the welfare of the family, and for your own welfare, O delightful one.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā tu tāṃ kanyāṃ kuntibhojo mahāyaśāḥ pṛthāṃ paridadau tasmai dvijāya sutavatsalaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus to that maiden, the greatly renowned Kuntibhoja, tender toward his daughter, entrusted Pṛthā to that brahmin.

sanskrit: iyaṃ brahman mama sutā bālā sukhavivardhitā aparādhyeta yat kiṃ cin na tat kāryaṃ hṛdi tvayā
english: This, O brahmin, is my daughter, a child raised in comfort. Whatever small offence she might commit — you must not take it to heart.

sanskrit: dvijātayo mahābhāgā vṛddhabālatapasviṣu bhavanty akrodhanāḥ prāyo viruddheṣv api nityadā
english: Twice-born of great fortune are generally free of anger toward the aged, children, and ascetics — even toward those who have wronged them — always.

sanskrit: sumahaty aparādhe 'pi kṣāntiḥ kāryā dvijātibhiḥ yathāśakti yathotsāhaṃ pūjā grāhyā dvijottama
english: Even for very great offences, forbearance is appropriate for the twice-born. And the honour given according to ability and eagerness should be accepted, O best of twice-born.

sanskrit: tatheti brāhmaṇenokte sa rājā prītamānasaḥ haṃsacandrāṃśusaṃkāśaṃ gṛham asya nyavedayat
english: When the brahmin said "So be it," the king, his mind rejoiced, assigned to him a house white as a swan and as the moon's rays.

sanskrit: tatrāgniśaraṇe kḷptam āsanaṃ tasya bhānumat āhārādi ca sarvaṃ tat tathaiva pratyavedayat
english: There in the fire-room, a bright seat was arranged for him, and all provisions of food and the rest were also made ready accordingly.

sanskrit: nikṣipya rājaputrī tu tandrīṃ mānaṃ tathaiva ca ātasthe paramaṃ yatnaṃ brāhmaṇasyābhirādhane
english: The princess, casting off all lethargy and pride, devoted herself with the utmost care to the service and honour of the brahmin.

sanskrit: tatra sā brāhmaṇaṃ gatvā pṛthā śaucaparā satī vidhivat paricārārhaṃ devavat paryatoṣayat
english: Going there to the brahmin, Pṛthā, chaste and devoted to purity, attended upon him who was worthy of service and gratified him according to the proper rites, as if he were a god.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sā tu kanyā mahārāja brāhmaṇaṃ saṃśitavratam toṣayām āsa śuddhena manasā saṃśitavratā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: That maiden, O great king, steadfast in her vows, gratified the brahmin who was firm in his vows, with a pure mind.

sanskrit: prātar āyāsya ity uktvā kadā cid dvijasattamaḥ tata āyāti rājendra sāye rātrāv atho punaḥ
english: Sometimes the best of twice-born, having said he would come in the morning, would then arrive in the evening, or again at night, O lord of kings.

sanskrit: taṃ ca sarvāsu velāsu bhakṣyabhojyapratiśrayaiḥ pūjayām āsa sā kanyā vardhamānais tu sarvadā
english: And at all these hours she, the maiden, would honour him with food, drink, and hospitality, ever increasing in her service, always.

sanskrit: annādisamudācāraḥ śayyāsanakṛtas tathā divase divase tasya vardhate na tu hīyate
english: The proper provision of food and other things, and the arrangement of his bed and seat — day by day these only grew and were never diminished.

sanskrit: nirbhartsanāpavādaiś ca tathaivāpriyayā girā brāhmaṇasya pṛthā rājan na cakārāpriyaṃ tadā
english: Even when rebuked or blamed, or spoken to with unpleasant words by the brahmin, Pṛthā did nothing displeasing to him at that time, O king.

sanskrit: vyaste kāle punaś caiti na caiti bahuśo dvijaḥ durlabhyam api caivānnaṃ dīyatām iti so 'bravīt
english: At inconvenient times the twice-born would arrive or often not arrive at all, and he would say, "Provide even what is hard to obtain."

sanskrit: kṛtam eva ca tat sarvaṃ pṛthā tasmai nyavedayat śiṣyavat putravac caiva svasṛvac ca susaṃyatā
english: And all of that Pṛthā accomplished and presented to him — with full composure, like a student, like a daughter, like a sister.

sanskrit: yathopajoṣaṃ rājendra dvijātipravarasya sā prītim utpādayām āsa kanyā yatnair aninditā
english: According to his pleasure, O lord of kings, that blameless maiden produced delight in the best of twice-born through her diligent efforts.

sanskrit: tasyās tu śīlavṛttena tutoṣa dvijasattamaḥ avadhānena bhūyo 'sya paraṃ yatnam athākarot
english: The best of brahmins was satisfied by her conduct and character, and with attentiveness he thereafter made even greater effort on her behalf.

sanskrit: tāṃ prabhāte ca sāye ca pitā papraccha bhārata api tuṣyati te putri brāhmaṇaḥ paricaryayā
english: Her father would ask her morning and evening, O descendant of Bharata: "Is the brahmin pleased with your service, my daughter?"

sanskrit: taṃ sā paramam ity eva pratyuvāca yaśasvinī tataḥ prītim avāpāgryāṃ kuntibhojo mahāmanāḥ
english: She, the renowned one, would always reply to him "Greatly so," and thereupon Kuntibhoja of great spirit attained supreme joy.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃvatsare pūrṇe yadāsau japatāṃ varaḥ nāpaśyad duṣkṛtaṃ kiṃ cit pṛthāyāḥ sauhṛde rataḥ
english: Then, when a full year had passed, that best of those who recite sacred texts, devoted to friendship with her, saw not a single fault in Pṛthā.

sanskrit: tataḥ prītamanā bhūtvā sa enāṃ brāhmaṇo 'bravīt prīto 'smi paramaṃ bhadre paricāreṇa te śubhe
english: Then, his mind rejoiced, the brahmin said to her: "I am supremely delighted by your service to me, O auspicious and gentle one."

sanskrit: varān vṛṇīṣva kalyāṇi durāpān mānuṣair iha yais tvaṃ sīmantinīḥ sarvā yaśasābhibhaviṣyasi
english: "Choose boons, O fortunate one — boons difficult for humans to obtain — by which you shall surpass all women of noble families in glory."

sanskrit: kunty uvāca kṛtāni mama sarvāṇi yasyā me vedavittama tvaṃ prasannaḥ pitā caiva kṛtaṃ vipra varair mama
english: Kuntī said: All things have been accomplished for me since you are pleased with me, O best knower of the Vedas. And by your boons my father's purpose is fulfilled, O brahmin.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca yadi necchasi bhadre tvaṃ varaṃ mattaḥ śucismite imaṃ mantraṃ gṛhāṇa tvam āhvānāya divaukasām
english: The brahmin said: If you do not wish a boon from me, O gentle and bright-smiling one, then take this mantra for the summoning of the gods.

sanskrit: yaṃ yaṃ devaṃ tvam etena mantreṇāvāhayiṣyasi tena tena vaśe bhadre sthātavyaṃ te bhaviṣyati
english: "Whichever god you summon with this mantra, O gentle one, that very god shall be obliged to be under your command."

sanskrit: akāmo vā sakāmo vā na sa naiṣyati te vaśam vibudho mantrasaṃśānto vākye bhṛtya ivānataḥ
english: "Whether willing or unwilling, that divine being, calmed by the mantra's power, shall not escape your control but shall bow to your word like a servant."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca na śaśāka dvitīyaṃ sā pratyākhyātum aninditā taṃ vai dvijātipravaraṃ tadā śāpabhayān nṛpa
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: She, the blameless one, was unable to refuse again that best of twice-born — out of fear of a curse, O king.

sanskrit: tatas tām anavadyāṅgīṃ grāhayām āsa vai dvijaḥ mantragrāmaṃ tadā rājann atharvaśirasi śrutam
english: Then the brahmin caused that woman of flawless limbs to receive that whole collection of mantras, O king, as heard in the Atharvāṅgiras.

sanskrit: taṃ pradāya tu rājendra kuntibhojam uvāca ha uṣito 'smi sukhaṃ rājan kanyayā paritoṣitaḥ
english: Having given it, O lord of kings, he spoke to Kuntibhoja: "I have dwelt happily, O king, fully satisfied by your daughter."

sanskrit: tava gehe suvihitaṃ sadā supratipūjitaḥ sādhayiṣyāmahe tāvad ity uktvāntaradhīyata
english: "Well provided for in your house, always well honoured — we shall now proceed with our purpose." Having said this, he vanished.

sanskrit: sa tu rājā dvijaṃ dṛṣṭvā tatraivāntarhitaṃ tadā babhūva vismayāviṣṭaḥ pṛthāṃ ca samapūjayat
english: The king, seeing that brahmin vanish right there and then, was filled with wonder, and he honoured Pṛthā deeply.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca gate tasmin dvijaśreṣṭhe kasmiṃś cit kālaparyaye cintayām āsa sā kanyā mantragrāmabalābalam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: After that best of twice-born had departed, at some point in the course of time, the maiden began to reflect on the power of the collection of mantras.

sanskrit: ayaṃ vai kīdṛśas tena mama datto mahātmanā mantragrāmo balaṃ tasya jñāsye nāticirād iva
english: "What is this collection of mantras given to me by that great-souled one? I shall come to know its power before too long."

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃcintayantī sā dadarśartuṃ yadṛcchayā vrīḍitā sābhavad bālā kanyābhāve rajasvalā
english: While thinking thus, she happened by chance to observe the season; abashed, the young girl, still in her maidenhood, became a woman in her menses.

sanskrit: athodyantaṃ sahasrāṃśuṃ pṛthā dīptaṃ dadarśa ha na tatarpa ca rūpeṇa bhānoḥ saṃdhyāgatasya sā
english: Then Pṛthā beheld the blazing sun with its thousand rays as it rose, and she could not be satisfied with the form of the sun as it rested in the twilight.

sanskrit: tasyā dṛṣṭir abhūd divyā sāpaśyad divyadarśanam āmuktakavacaṃ devaṃ kuṇḍalābhyāṃ vibhūṣitam
english: Her sight became divine and she saw a divine vision — the god wearing his armour and adorned with his earrings.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ kautūhalaṃ tv āsīn mantraṃ prati narādhipa āhvānam akarot sātha tasya devasya bhāminī
english: Curiosity arose in her regarding the mantra, O lord of men, and the spirited woman then made the invocation of that god.

sanskrit: prāṇān upaspṛśya tadā ājuhāva divākaram ājagāma tato rājaṃs tvaramāṇo divākaraḥ
english: Having sipped the breath, she invoked the maker of day; and then, O king, the maker of day came swiftly.

sanskrit: madhupiṅgo mahābāhuḥ kambugrīvo hasann iva aṅgadī baddhamukuṭo diśaḥ prajvālayann iva
english: Honey-golden, great-armed, with a throat like a conch, appearing to smile, wearing armlets and with a bound crown, blazing the directions as if on fire.

sanskrit: yogāt kṛtvā dvidhātmānam ājagāma tatāpa ca ābabhāṣe tataḥ kuntīṃ sāmnā paramavalgunā
english: Having divided himself in two through his yogic power, he came and blazed, and then addressed Kuntī with a voice supremely sweet and gentle.

sanskrit: āgato 'smi vaśaṃ bhadre tava mantrabalātkṛtaḥ kiṃ karomy avaśo rājñi brūhi kartā tad asmi te
english: "I have come under your power, O gentle one, compelled by the force of your mantra. What shall I do, O queen? Having no choice, tell me — I shall do it for you."

sanskrit: kunty uvāca gamyatāṃ bhagavaṃs tatra yato 'si samupāgataḥ kautūhalāt samāhūtaḥ prasīda bhagavann iti
english: Kuntī said: Go, O reverend one, back to where you came from. You were summoned out of mere curiosity. Be gracious, O reverend one.

sanskrit: sūrya uvāca gamiṣye 'haṃ yathā māṃ tvaṃ bravīṣi tanumadhyame na tu devaṃ samāhūya nyāyyaṃ preṣayituṃ vṛthā
english: The Sun said: I shall go as you say, O slender-waisted one. But it is not proper to summon a god and then dismiss him in vain.

sanskrit: tavābhisaṃdhiḥ subhage sūryāt putro bhaved iti vīryeṇāpratimo loke kavacī kuṇḍalīti ca
english: "Your intent, O fortunate one, is this: 'May there be a son from the Sun' — one unmatched in valour in the world, bearing armour and earrings."

sanskrit: sā tvam ātmapradānaṃ vai kuruṣva gajagāmini utpatsyati hi putras te yathāsaṃkalpam aṅgane
english: "Therefore, O woman with the gait of an elephant, give yourself over; for a son shall be born to you, O fair courtyard-dwelling one, exactly as you intended."

sanskrit: atha gacchāmy ahaṃ bhadre tvayāsaṃgamya susmite śapsyāmi tvām ahaṃ kruddho brāhmaṇaṃ pitaraṃ ca te
english: "But if I go, O gentle and bright-smiling one, without uniting with you, I shall curse you in my anger, and your brahmin father as well."

sanskrit: tvatkṛte tān pradhakṣyāmi sarvān api na saṃśayaḥ pitaraṃ caiva te mūḍhaṃ yo na vetti tavānayam
english: "On your account I shall burn them all — without doubt — including your foolish father who does not understand the impropriety you have done."

sanskrit: tasya ca brāhmaṇasyādya yo 'sau mantram adāt tava śīlavṛttam avijñāya dhāsyāmi vinayaṃ param
english: "And that brahmin who gave you the mantra without knowing your character and conduct — I shall today impart supreme punishment to him."

sanskrit: ete hi vibudhāḥ sarve puraṃdaramukhā divi tvayā pralabdhaṃ paśyanti smayanta iva bhāmini
english: "For all these gods in heaven, led by Indra, behold you mocking them as it were, O passionate one, and they are smiling."

sanskrit: paśya cainān suragaṇān divyaṃ cakṣur idaṃ hi te pūrvam eva mayā dattaṃ dṛṣṭavaty asi yena mām
english: "Look at these hosts of gods — this divine eye is yours, given by me even before; it is by means of this that you saw me."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato 'paśyat tridaśān rājaputrī; sarvān eva sveṣu dhiṣṇyeṣu khasthān prabhāsantaṃ bhānumantaṃ mahāntaṃ; yathādityaṃ rocamānaṃ tathaiva
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the king's daughter saw the thirty gods, all of them stationed in their places in the sky, and the great luminous sun shining just as the Āditya shines.

sanskrit: sā tān dṛṣṭvā vrīḍamāneva bālā; sūryaṃ devī vacanaṃ prāha bhītā gaccha tvaṃ vai gopate svaṃ vimānaṃ; kanyābhāvād duḥkha eṣopacāraḥ
english: Seeing them, the young woman, the goddess, abashed and afraid, spoke to the Sun: "Go to your own chariot, O lord of cattle. This solicitation is a hardship for one still a maiden."

sanskrit: pitā mātā guravaś caiva ye 'nye; dehasyāsya prabhavanti pradāne nāhaṃ dharmaṃ lopayiṣyāmi loke; strīṇāṃ vṛttaṃ pūjyate deharakṣā
english: "Father, mother, and teachers, and whatever others have authority over the giving of this body — I shall not transgress dharma in the world. The conduct of women is honoured as the protection of their body."
